column1: # CLOSED INVENTORY of every control case scripts/test-doc-evidence.sh emits.
# WHY. The coverage runner mapped 22 named fragments to mutations and called the controls
# non-vacuous. There were 64. Deleting an unmapped one changed no baseline failure and had
# no mutation identity, so the runner stayed green -- the claim was wider than the
# measurement, for the third time on this branch. Now every control has a declared role,
# reconciled BOTH WAYS against the labels the script prints AT RUNTIME, so a control cannot
# be deleted, renamed, or silently stop running without this file failing.
# The list below is reconciled against what `bash scripts/test-doc-evidence.sh` prints, and
# that one command is also how a reviewer reproduces every case and its verdict:
#   bash scripts/test-doc-evidence.sh
# `make test-doc-evidence-coverage` then reverts each fix and reports which case notices.
# Columns are TAB-separated: case-label  role  detail
#   kill  <mutation>   reverting that mutation MUST make this case fail, checked by name --
#                      a mutation that reddens three unrelated cases while leaving this one
#                      passing is WRONG-CONTROL, not coverage.
#   guard <reason>     a green-side control, there to stop the gate becoming OVER-strict. No
#                      mutation makes it fail, and that is its job; the role is declared so
#                      "nothing kills it" is a statement rather than a gap.
a TRUE index passes (count, absence, PIPELINE, find expr, conformance)
column3: the fatal green control: if it fails, detection cannot be told from breakage
